messages:
mari: Quick heads-up — ran a small FP8 pass this morning on the customer QA set and saw ~2.4% BLEU drop vs our int8 baseline. Not catastrophic but noticeable. Anyone else seeing FP8 quality deltas?
bench-bot: Automated run 1758449201 queued by @mari for model=resnet-like-qa quant=fp8 dataset=customer_qa seed=42. Outputs will upload to /bench/runs/1758449201.
alex: Hmm, thanks for flagging. Can you paste the exact commit + quant config you used? Also which eval slices (long context, code, tables)? :eyes:
mari: Commit is 9a7d2b3 (quant/kernels: fp8 path tweak). Eval was the full customer_qa split but skewed to long-context questions (~30% > 1024 tokens). Config snippet: ```quant: { type: "fp8", scaling: "per-tensor", rounding: "nearest" } batch_size: 8 max_len: 1536```
sam: I saw something similar yesterday on a different model — FP8 seemed fine for short contexts but degraded on long-context QA answers (hallucinated facts). Worth checking KV cache handling and kernel edge-case when sequence > block size.
priyanka: @alex can you run a profiler + logits diff vs int8 on the failing samples? simplest metric: mean L2 diff of logits and delta in top-1 accuracy. If we see systematic bias we can blame scaling.
alex: Will do. Queuing a profile job for the same commit + seed. Command I’ll run: ```./bench/run_eval.sh --model-ref=9a7d2b3 --quant=fp8 --dataset=customer_qa --seed=42 --profile=trace.json --compare=int8``` Should get first traces in ~20m.
infra-bot: Job 1758449450 started on gpu-pool-a (p3-8). Estimated completion 22m.
bench-bot: Job 1758449450 finished. Summary: throughput=220 tok/s (fp8) vs 180 tok/s (int8); latency p95 improved ~18%. Artifacts: /bench/runs/1758449450/{trace.json,logits_diff.csv,eval_summary.json}
mari: Thanks. Can you paste the eval_summary numbers? Especially BLEU/EM/ROUGE deltas.
bench-bot: eval_summary.json excerpt: fp8 vs int8 -> BLEU: -2.4, EM: -1.1, ROUGE-L: -1.8. Logit mean L2 diff on failing subset: 0.032, top-1 swap rate: 3.6%.
alex: Log profiler shows quant scaling factor flips around token 1024 for several layers — looks like a per-chunk rescale was applied inconsistently during KV merge. Attaching short trace excerpt: ```trace excerpt: layer12.scaling: [0.125,0.125,0.25,0.25] at token indices [1008..1032] -> unexpected jump```
priyanka: That matches my hypothesis. @mari did the kernel tweak include a merge path for partial blocks? If not we may be applying scaling twice on the tail.
mari: The change was to add an FP8 fast-path that assumed full blocks; I missed the partial-block branch. Ugh. I can open a revert PR or push a fix. Thoughts on rollback vs patch? :thinking_face:
sam: If this affects customer QA we should canary rollback the fast-path while we patch. Rollback is lower risk and buys time.
alex: I can open a quick PR to restore previous kernel behavior (no fast-path) and add a unit test for partial-blocks. Will include profiler traces and bench results.
infrastructure-bump: (ops note) if we revert, we should also trigger a canary perf run to ensure we don't regress throughput too much for dedicated customers.
mari: Ok let's rollback the fast-path for now. @alex please assign to @priyanka for review when ready. I'll also put a note in the release notes and flag the Dedicated clusters.
alex: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3124 — title: "revert(fp8): disable fast-path for partial-block KV merge". Includes test + trace. Marking reviewers: priyanka, mari. :shipit:
priyanka: Reviewing now. Quick suggestion: add a small fuzz test where seq_len mod block_size != 0 with random scaling to catch future regressions.
bench-bot: Canary run 1758449712 (post-revert) finished. Summary: BLEU delta vs int8 now -0.2, throughput loss vs pre-revert fp8 fast-path: -5%. Artifacts: /bench/runs/1758449712/eval_summary.json
mari: That looks acceptable. We'll keep FP8 enabled but without fast-path until we can add robust partial-block handling. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :pray:
alex: Will follow up with a PR to reintroduce fast-path behind a feature flag + extensive tests.
priyanka: I'll add the fuzz tests to our quant test suite.
infra-bot: Noting: inform customers on Dedicated upgrade channel about temporary rollback and perf note.
mari: Leaving this thread open for any follow-ups. If you spot more edge cases ping here. :eyes:
